issues.problem: When the file parses, only the parsed structure is used. strip_jsonc ends a // comment only at \n, but VS Code's JSONC scanner (jsonc-parser isLineBreak) also ends it at \r. A CR after a // comment therefore makes the checker drop a runOptions/allowAutomaticTasks member that VS Code applies. 647e27b (regex on decoded text) still flagged this payload, so the new parser is weaker for it.
issues.evidence: REVF-H3c-probe/wormcr: a/.vscode/tasks.json = '{"version": "2.0.0", "tasks": [{"label": "x", "type": "shell", "command": "echo pwn" // c\r, "runOptions": {"runOn": "folderOpen"}\n}]}' and b/.vscode/settings.json = '{"editor.tabSize": 2 // c\r, "task.allowAutomaticTasks": "on"\n}'. check-repo-invariants.sh --check worm-indicators: 6c57daa -> 'PASS worm-indicators' rc=0; 647e27b -> FAIL, both files reported.
issues.suggested_fix: End // comments at \r as well as \n. Also report the union of the parsed walk and the decoded-text regexes, so a divergence between strip_jsonc and VS Code can never hide a literal "runOn": "folderOpen". Add the CR case to WormIndicatorsTest.

issues.problem: A tracked .vscode/*.json saved with a UTF-8 BOM (Windows editors do this; VS Code reads it fine) is now reported as 'cannot be parsed as JSON with comments' and fails the invariant. Before this commit it passed.
issues.evidence: REVF-H3c-probe/wormbom: printf '\xef\xbb\xbf{"recommendations": ["ms-python.python"]}' > a/.vscode/extensions.json -> 'FAIL worm-indicators  a/.vscode/extensions.json: cannot be parsed as JSON with comments ...' (json.loads: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM).
issues.suggested_fix: Decode with 'utf-8-sig'. Add a BOM case to test_ordinary_config_and_unrelated_files_pass.

issues.problem: (a) False positive. The quoted-key and flow-step test runs before the run-script skip, so honest script content is rejected: a JSON heredoc in a 'run: |' block ("ref": "main") or a '- {' line in a with: literal block. No test covers the honest variant. (b) Bypass. Flow-mapping jobs and steps still evade: 'build: {runs-on: ..., continue-on-error: true, steps: [{run: echo ok}]}' and 'steps: [{run: ''echo ${{ github.event.issue.title }}'', continue-on-error: true}]' return no problems. For a flow job, the timeout-minutes check is skipped too.
issues.evidence: python3 -I REVF-H3c-probe/wf/probe_wf.py (output in wf/out.txt): json-heredoc-in-run -> ['...:15: quoted keys and flow-style steps hide settings ...']; yaml-list-in-with-body -> same; job-level flow mapping continue-on-error -> []; steps flow sequence -> [].
issues.suggested_fix: Apply QUOTED_KEY/FLOW_STEP only outside run scripts and block scalars (after the script_until skip), and add an honest-heredoc test. Reject any flow mapping or sequence ('{' or '[') as the value of a key under jobs:, or simply any line whose value starts with '{' or '[' outside scripts.

issues.problem: Bare paths are matched only as tokens that start with hooks/ or scripts/. A project-relative script chained after a valid plugin-root script still passes when written as ./hooks/..., $PWD/hooks/... or ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/scripts/.... All 96 real commands have exactly the form "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/<file>".
issues.evidence: REVF-H3c-probe/hookref fixture, --check hook-references: 'bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/a.sh" && bash ./hooks/evil.sh' -> PASS rc=0; '... && bash "$PWD/hooks/evil.sh"' -> PASS; '... && bash ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/scripts/evil.sh' -> PASS (the r2 form '... && bash hooks/evil.sh' now fails correctly).
issues.suggested_fix: Use an allowlist: every command must match ^"\$\{CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT\}/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+"( [A-Za-z0-9._=-]+)*$ with an existing file, and fail on anything else. Test the three forms above.

issues.problem: The new 'trap ... EXIT' replaces the one at line 53, so $TMP is no longer removed. The leak is contained under run-all-tests.sh's sandboxed TMPDIR, but a direct run leaves a directory behind each time.
issues.evidence: grep -n trap tests/scripts/test-verify-release-commit-ci.sh -> 53: trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT; 110: trap 'rm -rf "$derive_root"' EXIT.
issues.suggested_fix: trap 'rm -rf "$TMP" "$derive_root"' EXIT, or create derive_root under $TMP.
